solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Christian caught on the microphone

indicators.note: words spoken into a microphone are heard rather than read, so the letters entered only match the spoken word in sound

parts.note: to be copped is slang for being caught, as by the police

explanation.surface: A believer is arrested and overheard on a bugged line or a radio mic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt is a member of the ancient Egyptian church, so a Christian of that tradition.

clue.text: Mischievous tricks conveyed by hypocrisy with tears

parts.note: cant is insincere, pious talk
rips and tears are both splits in fabric

explanation.surface: Pranks are carried out with false piety and fake crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' is read as rents in cloth, not crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for spells or witchcraft, extended to mischievous pranks.

clue.text: A pro in long dress

indicators.note: A and the word for pro go into the word for long

parts.note: to pine is to long for
pro means in favour of, so for

explanation.surface: A professional sports a long gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless garment worn over a blouse, a type of frock.

clue.text: Two perhaps yet further up the scale of insensitivity

parts.note: even and yet both intensify a comparison: even more, yet more

parts.words: further up the scale of insensitivity
parts.note: numb means without feeling, so the comparative, more numb, is spelt as a word for further along that scale

explanation.surface: Someone is described as twice as callous and climbing higher still on a scale of unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read as NUMB-ER, the comparative of numb, not as the noun for a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is an example of a figure divisible by two, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Bear witness giving very short cry of pain

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, so very short gives that letter
ouch is what one shouts when hurt

explanation.surface: A witness in court gives a brief yelp of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch is to attest or confirm something as true.

clue.text: Article taken in arrest registered as food

indicators.note: the article is taken into the word for arrest

parts.note: to nab is to catch or arrest
an is the indefinite article
a meter that read a value has registered it

explanation.surface: An item seized in a police arrest is logged as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan bread is a leavened flatbread from South Asia, a kind of food.

clue.text: Appear in rags maybe around university, as one unwillingly constrained

indicators.note: the dressing word goes round the university's letter

parts.note: to underdress is to wear clothes too shabby for the occasion, rags being an extreme example

explanation.surface: A student turns up at college in tatters, plainly forced into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting under compulsion or threat means doing so because one is coerced.

clue.text: Former enemy of Good Eng.? A beast!

parts.note: the opposite, the enemy, of good is bad
England's former wartime enemy was Germany, abbreviated GER as England is to Eng.

explanation.surface: A wartime foe of 'Good England' is condemned as a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Good Eng.' as a label; its enemy is the opposing label 'Bad Ger.', bad against good and Germany against England.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger is a burrowing nocturnal mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Revolutionary soldiers rising kill folk in privileged family

indicators.note: turning right round, the soldiers' letters are read the other way

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to slay is to kill

explanation.surface: Rebel troops rise up to kill members of a pampered household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns OR into RO and 'rising' turns SLAY into YALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a monarch's household are the most privileged of families.

clue.text: Square symbolically seen here

parts.note: the clue's own number in the grid is 9, a square number (three times three), written as a symbol right beside the clue

explanation.surface: Someone points at a square symbol printed on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' is the clue's label: this is clue 9, and the figure 9 is a perfect square.
explanation.definitionFit: Three multiplied by itself gives this perfect square, and its numeral labels this very clue.

clue.text: Drug addict half gone, say — unfortunate fellow preying on youngster?

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters are knocked into a new order
with half its letters gone, only the front half of the word addict is kept

explanation.surface: A drug addict, half wasted, is pitied as a poor wretch who preys on the young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' rearranges DRUG, ADD (the first half of 'addict') and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy older man who lavishes gifts on a much younger lover is sometimes seen as exploiting them.

clue.text: Flashy females one spots outside?

indicators.note: the word for spots wraps round the other pieces, sitting outside them

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man asks whether flashy women are the sort who spot someone outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish describes a showy, disreputable style, rakishly unconventional and vulgarly bright.

clue.text: Difficult month as bill is put aside for future consideration

indicators.note: a difficult text is a twisted one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hard month in which an unpaid invoice is shelved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes stored away with camphor balls are kept for later use; figuratively, a plan shelved for the time being.

clue.text: Simple fare, see — duck sacrificed to be consumed by heathen god

indicators.note: the trimmed see is eaten, placed inside the god's name

parts.note: Baal is the Canaanite deity denounced in the Old Testament

indicators.note: the duck is given up, removed from the see's letters

parts.note: the Holy See is in Rome, so a see can be the city itself
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A plain meal offered to a pagan god, with a duck slaughtered for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the Vatican in Rome; 'sacrificed' removes the duck's letter from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served in a pub at the counter is cheap, unfussy fare.

clue.text: It could be Oxbridge bag

definitions.meaning: Oxbridge blends Oxford and Cambridge, an example of a blended word
a large travelling case opening into two halves

explanation.surface: A university trunk carried up to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a blend word, coined by Lewis Carroll, and a hinged two-part suitcase.

clue.text: Fellow human being from which no rough sound is heard

indicators.note: the pair of words is spoken, so only their sound matters

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, and a burr is a rough rolled R in some accents

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow creature from whom no harsh noise ever comes.
explanation.walkthrough: A burr is the rough rolled R of West Country or Scots speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving one's neighbour, in the Gospel sense, means any fellow human.

clue.text: Sitting on mountains, Parisian is cut off

indicators.note: in a down light, the French word sits on top of the mountains

parts.note: est is French for is
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A Parisian perched on high peaks is isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, separating them from others.

clue.text: Contrary Scot Roy managed to undermine a new US city

indicators.note: in a down light, the reversed pieces go under the first two letters
contrary means going the other way, so the outlaw and the verb are read backwards

parts.note: Rob Roy MacGregor was a Scottish outlaw, so Roy the Scot is Rob
to run something is to manage it, so ran

explanation.surface: A perverse Scot named Roy plots to topple a newly founded American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' turns ROB RAN into NARBOR; Rob Roy is Scotland's Robin Hood figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann Arbor is a city in Michigan, home of its state university.

clue.text: Cain? Possibly him

definitions.meaning: Cain was born after Adam and Eve, so he was the third human in Genesis
him is an example of the grammatical category for someone neither speaking nor addressed

explanation.surface: A question about Cain, and a guess that he is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve came first, so Cain was the next human; grammatically, he and him belong to this category.

clue.text: Soldier turning up in place of entertainment gets a plug

indicators.note: the reversed soldier goes inside the venue

parts.note: a nightspot or hot spot is a venue for fun

indicators.note: in a down light, turning up means reading the soldier's letters from the bottom

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier turns up at a nightclub and gets plugged, or gets a publicity plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or stopper that closes the vent of a cask.

clue.text: Island that has suffered in need of love

parts.note: something borne has been endured or suffered
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An island that has been through hardship and lacks love.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the large island in the Malay Archipelago, shared by three nations.

clue.text: Bumptious official, poor speller given a word of contempt

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh says his spelling is wobbly, the classic crossword poor speller
bah is an exclamation of scorn

explanation.surface: A self-important official, bad at spelling, is dismissed with a sneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh, the bear in A. A. Milne's stories, admits his spelling is wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the pompous many-titled character in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado now means any self-important functionary.

clue.text: A short ordeal involving America or some other country

indicators.note: the first pieces take in the abbreviation for America
cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a test of endurance
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A brief hardship takes in the United States or some other nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a central European nation, a land other than America.

clue.text: Something sung, last bit of hymn, following church regarded as heretical

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word hymn is used

explanation.surface: A hymn sung in church ends on a note thought heretical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church' sits inside the definition; it is not CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Arius denied Christ's full divinity, a view the early Church condemned as heresy.

clue.text: Famous person among group of workers in charge of nerve centre

indicators.note: the celebrity sits in among the workers' group and the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a gang is a team of labourers
a literary lion is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity mixes with a crew of workers who run a control hub.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells acting as a relay hub, and this adjective describes it.

clue.text: Singular bigwig who may look down on those deemed inferior?

definitions.text: who may look down on those deemed inferior?

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a nob is a person of wealth or high rank

explanation.surface: One particular grandee who sneers at people he thinks beneath him.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person despises those of lower class or taste, looking down their nose.

clue.text: Jean maybe stealing

definitions.meaning: jean is a heavy cotton twill, an example of cloth used to make trousers
to trouser money is to pocket it, often dishonestly

explanation.surface: A woman named Jean is perhaps a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean looks like a woman's name; it is the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fabric for making trousers, and also the act of pocketing money improperly.

clue.text: Good listener? Unusually good

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A good listener is praised as exceptionally good.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixties slang for great or fabulous, describing something exceptionally fine.
